$Comment: The Headless Horseman's hard ride: the same fight as Hallows_Eve_Headless_Horseman_Encounter, a
Variant of this pack's Orbis_Boss_Encounter_Template, with his hard forms and faster timings, the
way the game's own Gobliterator has a hard script beside its normal one. It runs in his hard
graveyard (Prefabs/Hallows_Eve/Hallows_Eve_Graveyard_Hard.prefab.json), where he rises from
Hallows_Eve_Headless_Horseman_Hard_Marker once players have beaten three waves of skeletons around
the fountain.
The waves before he rises are GuardWave, ziggfreed-common's Zc_Wave_Chain, set in
_ForwardedModifiers below. As players arrive (8 seconds on, once the intro camera is done), the
first wave rises: three Jack Skeletons on the plaza south of the fountain, 7 blocks north of the
fight's entity and spread across 90 degrees, and two Jack Archers at the fountain's north
corners, 19 blocks out across 37 degrees (every spot open floor in the hard graveyard), with no
toast. Once the last of a wave falls, the next rises 4 seconds later; if none of a wave is seen
within 3 seconds it counts as beaten, so a spot that fails never holds the fight. Players who
fall among the waves come back to the same wave. The chain holds Orbis_Boss_Guards_Pending,
which keeps him down, and its Waiting,
Up and Seen flags are the template's Orbis_Boss_Guards_ ones; its Done flag,
Orbis_Boss_Waves_Done, is one the template never clears, so once the three are beaten they stay
beaten after a wipe on him, and he rises again as players come back to the fountain. The waves
come from the Spawn action, so the hard graveyard's Mob Scaling band makes them tougher.
During his fight, each time he loses another fifth of his health (at 80, 60, 40 and 20 percent
of his maximum), his pumpkins hatch five Pumpkin Fiends (Hallows_Eve_Pumpkin_Fiend_Hatchling, the
wild fiend under an id of its own, so only the fight's fiends are in its adds group) across the
plaza where the waves' Jack
Skeletons stood, 7 blocks north of the fight's entity across 90 degrees, and two more Jack
Archers rise at the fountain's north corners, beside his own adds at the throw and at his wrath:
FightWaves, the pack's Macro_Orbis_Boss_Fight_Waves, also set below, which tells the members as
each hatches (Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Pumpkins). The normal ride hatches three fiends at a time. A
reset clears its flags, so every try raises them again.
What is harder lives in three places. His _HM roles carry more health (2376 against 1100, his
Head 450 against 300), the Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Hard_Mode effect, which makes everything he
swings or throws hit 40% harder, and in the saddle a lantern bomb he aims at a player for 3
seconds before he throws it, the one bomb of the fight thrown straight at someone. His health
steps are the _Hard_Scale effects, 1080 per player beyond the first. And _ForwardedModifiers
below tightens the phases: a volley every 4 seconds from the start, each bomb leaving a fire
patch; he is thrown at 54.55% (1296 of 2376 solo, so the saddle holds 1080 of it); his head
first flies 6 seconds after his fall, then every 28 seconds, and returns after 20; his wrath,
at 30% (713 solo) and only once his head has flown, brings burning volleys every 6 seconds.
No health packs fall on this ride. The bar shows the game's hard-mode style (BossBarHardMode)
and his hard name.
Its reach is the normal fight's, since both graveyards are one place (that file tells the
distances): ArenaRange 61 and ScalePlayerRange count everyone in the graveyard and nobody in the
entrance room, CorpseRange 70 finds a fallen player anywhere in it, both kinds of volley reach
every player in the fight, and LeashRange 57 calls him back before he can follow anyone into the
entrance room. Change these with the normal fight's.
A win pays its own two Claims, Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Daily_Hard and Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Chase_Hard,
counted apart from the normal fight's, so a player can collect both on the same day. The binding
row ZiggfreedCommon/Encounters/Hallows_Eve_Headless_Horseman_Encounter_Hard.json names the fight
and keeps its records apart. This file's name is not a role's: a script named after a role
replaces it.
